clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A hospital hand-hygiene audit identifies repeated missed opportunities on one unit. Which follow-up action best aligns with the current CDC ICAR quality-improvement approach?

options.A: Share summarized audit findings with the unit and use the identified gaps to target performance improvement.
options.B: Stop auditing once a problem is identified because further monitoring does not contribute to improvement.
options.C: Use the audit findings only for disciplinary action and withhold them from the staff performing the work.
options.D: Treat one audit result as proof that every hand-hygiene opportunity on the unit is being performed incorrectly.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC's June 25, 2026 Infection Control Assessment and Response (ICAR) tool defines an audit as direct observation or monitoring of healthcare personnel adherence to job-specific infection-prevention measures. It defines feedback as a summary of audit findings used to target performance improvement. The ICAR framework is designed to systematically assess practices, identify gaps, and guide quality-improvement activities. Therefore, the appropriate response is to communicate the audit findings and use them to focus corrective improvement rather than stopping measurement, withholding feedback, or overgeneralizing one sample to every opportunity.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Use hand-hygiene audit findings as quality-improvement data: provide feedback and target identified adherence gaps rather than treating the audit as an endpoint or punitive measure alone.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: replaced a weakly source-bounded electronic-monitoring interpretation item with a current June 2026 CDC ICAR audit-and-feedback scenario that directly tests quality-improvement use of hand-hygiene adherence data; removed absolute wording and answer-length cueing.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original electronic-monitoring answer was uniquely long and depended on broad measurement-limitations claims not tightly bounded by the cited current source. The revised item uses current CDC definitions with a directly supported quality-improvement decision.

option_audit.A: Correct. It matches CDC's definition of feedback and the ICAR purpose of using identified gaps to guide quality improvement.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. ICAR uses assessment and monitoring to support improvement rather than ending measurement after the first gap is found.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. CDC defines feedback as a summary of audit findings used to target performance improvement, not information to be withheld from staff as a purely punitive tool.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. An audit sample identifies adherence gaps but does not establish that every opportunity on the unit was performed incorrectly.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone applies the current CDC audit-feedback-quality-improvement framework to the identified hand-hygiene gap.
cueing_check: All four choices are follow-up actions after an audit and are comparable in length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
